lessons.title: Choose the Project Generator and Build Baseline

questions.title: Start from Spring Initializr
questions.question: Spring Initializr creates a Spring Boot project shell and lets us choose the build system, language, Java version, metadata, and dependencies before source files are generated. Which generator should we use to begin the PetClinic reconstruction?

questions.title: Choose Maven first
questions.question: PetClinic supports Maven and Gradle, but pom.xml is a primary build definition and gives us the first reproducible build path. Which build system should we select first?

questions.title: Choose Java
questions.question: Spring PetClinic is implemented in Java. Spring Initializr can generate Java, Kotlin, or Groovy projects. Which language should we select for this reconstruction?

questions.title: Use Java 17 as the baseline
questions.question: The canonical PetClinic project declares Java 17 as its baseline. Which Java version should we select so the generated project matches that build requirement?

questions.title: Set the PetClinic group
questions.question: Maven coordinates identify a project with a group and artifact. PetClinic source code lives under org.springframework.samples.petclinic, so which group value should we use before defining the artifact?

questions.title: Set the PetClinic artifact and package
questions.question: The project repository is named spring-petclinic, while the Java base package is org.springframework.samples.petclinic. Which artifact name should we enter now so the generated project carries the PetClinic project identity?

questions.title: Add Spring Web
questions.question: PetClinic is a server-rendered Spring MVC application. Spring Web provides the MVC request-handling infrastructure used by controllers and the embedded web application. Which dependency should we add first for the web layer?

questions.title: Add Spring Data JPA
questions.question: PetClinic persists owners, pets, visits, and veterinarians in relational databases. Spring Data JPA provides repository abstractions on top of JPA and Hibernate. Which dependency should we add for persistence?

questions.title: Add Validation
questions.question: PetClinic validates form data such as names, dates, and other domain inputs before accepting changes. Spring Boot's Validation dependency integrates Jakarta Bean Validation for these rules. Which dependency should we add?

questions.title: Set the project name to petclinic
questions.question: Maven uses the artifact ID for coordinates, but the project can also have a human-readable name. The canonical PetClinic pom.xml declares <name>petclinic</name>. Which project name should we enter so the generated project identity matches the finished application?

questions.title: Correct the Java base package
questions.question: Spring Boot component scanning normally starts from the package containing the application class. The canonical PetClinic Java source lives under org.springframework.samples.petclinic, so which package name should we set instead of the artifact-derived org.springframework.samples.springpetclinic?

questions.title: Keep JAR packaging
questions.question: Spring Boot can package an application as a JAR or WAR. PetClinic runs as a self-contained Spring Boot application with an embedded web server rather than being deployed as a traditional external-container WAR. Which packaging option should we keep selected?

questions.title: Use Properties configuration
questions.question: Spring Boot supports both .properties and YAML configuration. The canonical PetClinic repository uses application.properties together with profile-specific .properties files under src/main/resources. Which configuration format should the generated project use?

lessons.title: [EXPERIMENTAL — DELETE LATER] Java Constructors UI Action Test

questions.title: Inspect the no-argument object
questions.question: A constructor runs when an object is created. Here Human() assigns age 12 and name John before new Human() finishes. After `Human obj = new Human();`, what values should obj contain?

original_action.description: Observe an existing Human object that receives default values.

questions.title: Pass custom values during object creation
questions.question: To initialize a second Human with its own age and name at creation time, the arguments must be passed inside new Human(...). Which object-creation statement requests age 18 and name Naveen?

original_action.description: Create a second Human object while attempting to pass a custom age and name.

questions.title: Recognize the constructor mismatch
questions.question: Java matches constructor calls by their parameter lists. Human currently has no constructor accepting int and String, so why is `new Human(18, "Naveen")` invalid?
questions.answer: There is no matching Human(int, String) constructor yet.

problems.message: No matching constructor for Human(int, String)

original_action.description: Observe that the IDE reports an error because Human currently has no constructor accepting int and String.
original_action.expected_problem: No matching constructor for Human(int, String)

questions.title: Declare the matching parameterized constructor
questions.question: A constructor has the same name as its class and no return type. Which constructor signature can receive the int and String supplied by new Human(18, "Naveen")?

original_action.description: Create a constructor accepting an integer and a string.

questions.title: Store constructor parameters in fields
questions.question: Constructor parameters only hold the incoming values unless we copy them into the object's fields. What assignments make the new Human keep a and n as its age and name?

original_action.description: Assign the incoming constructor arguments to the object's fields.

questions.title: Trace arguments into object state
questions.question: In `new Human(18, "Naveen")`, arguments flow into constructor parameters and then fields. What is the complete value flow for the two arguments?
questions.answer: 18 → a → age, and Naveen → n → name.

original_action.description: Connect the values passed from new Human(18, "Naveen") to the constructor parameters.

questions.title: Compare constructor signatures
questions.question: Constructor overloading lets one class offer different initialization choices. Which signatures are selected by `new Human()` and `new Human(18, "Naveen")`?

original_action.description: Compare object creation without arguments to object creation with arguments.

questions.title: Duplicate the output statement
questions.question: To compare the two Human objects in the console, we need a second print statement before changing its variable. Which existing output line should be duplicated?

original_action.description: Create another output statement so values from both Human objects can be compared.

questions.title: Predict the first object's output
questions.question: The first object uses the no-argument constructor, which assigns age 12 and name John. What should its print statement display?

original_action.description: Print values belonging to the object created without arguments.

questions.title: Print the second object's values
questions.question: The duplicated print line still refers to obj. Which variable should the second print use so it displays the object created with 18 and Naveen?

original_action.description: Print values belonging to the object created with custom constructor arguments.

questions.title: Run the constructor example
questions.question: Running the program now tests whether the two constructor paths produce independent object state. What two lines should appear in the console?

data.name: HumanDemo
data.console:
12 : John
18 : Naveen

Process finished with exit code 0

original_action.description: Compile and run the application.

questions.title: Verify independent object values
questions.question: The console shows `12 : John` for obj and `18 : Naveen` for obj1. What does this demonstrate about constructor-based initialization?
questions.answer: Each object can receive and keep its own initialization values.

data.text:
12 : John
18 : Naveen

Process finished with exit code 0

original_action.description: Verify that the two objects contain different data.
original_action.learning_result: Each object can receive independent values through a constructor.

questions.title: Temporarily remove declared constructors
questions.question: Java supplies a no-argument constructor automatically only when the class declares no constructor. What should happen if we temporarily remove the explicitly declared constructors from Human?
questions.answer: The compiler can provide an implicit no-argument Human() constructor.

original_action.description: Remove or comment the explicitly declared constructor to demonstrate Java's automatic constructor behavior.

questions.title: Identify the compiler-provided constructor
questions.question: With no constructor declared in Human, Java provides a default constructor. What is its conceptual no-argument form?

original_action.description: Explain that when no constructor is declared, Java automatically supplies a no-argument constructor.

questions.title: Open IntelliJ constructor generation
questions.question: Instead of typing constructor boilerplate manually, IntelliJ can generate it from class fields. Which IDE feature should we open?

original_action.description: Use the IDE's source/code generation capability to generate constructors.

questions.title: Choose fields for the generated constructor
questions.question: To generate the constructor that accepts both object properties, which fields should be selected in the constructor-generation dialog?

original_action.description: Select age and name so the IDE generates a constructor accepting both fields.

questions.title: Generate the two-parameter constructor
questions.question: When IntelliJ generates a constructor for age and name, parameter names can match field names. Which assignments distinguish the current object's fields from those parameters?

original_action.description: Allow the IDE to generate a constructor containing age and name parameters.

questions.title: Generate a no-argument constructor
questions.question: The class can overload constructors by using different parameter lists. Which additional constructor lets callers create a Human without passing any arguments?

original_action.description: Use the IDE constructor-generation feature again to create a no-argument constructor.

questions.title: Add defaults to the no-argument constructor
questions.question: An explicitly written no-argument constructor can choose its own starting values. What values should it assign to reproduce the original default Human state?

original_action.description: Add predefined values to the no-argument constructor.

questions.title: Understand this inside a constructor
questions.question: When a constructor parameter has the same name as a field, `this` refers to the current object. In `this.age = age`, what does the left-side `this.age` mean?
questions.answer: The age field belonging to the current Human object.

original_action.description: Compare parameter names with instance-variable names and explain why this is used.

questions.title: Generate a name-only overloaded constructor
questions.question: Constructor overloading can also accept only selected values. Which constructor signature lets callers provide a name while leaving age to another initialization rule?

original_action.description: Use the IDE generation feature to create another constructor accepting only name.

questions.title: Create an object with the name-only constructor
questions.question: Now that Human(String name) exists, which statement creates a third object by supplying only Naveen?

original_action.description: Create another Human object by supplying only the name.

questions.title: Predict the uninitialized int field
questions.question: Human(String name) assigns name but does not assign age. Java instance int fields default to 0, so what value does obj2.age have at this point?

data.message: obj2.age = 0 because the name-only constructor has not assigned age.

original_action.description: Explain that age remains 0 when the constructor does not assign a value to it.

questions.title: Give the name-only constructor a custom default age
questions.question: A constructor can supply an internal default for a value the caller did not provide. What assignment should we add so Human("Naveen") receives age 12?

original_action.description: Modify the single-name constructor so objects created with only a name receive age 12.
